title: A Safe, Reliable, and Resilient Rail System
what_it_is: A Safe, Reliable, and Resilient Rail System

sections.label: East-West Line disruption impact
sections.summary: The 25 September East-West Line disruption affected about 500,000 of 2.8 million daily train-based passenger journeys, causing significant commuter inconvenience.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
sentences.text: The severe disruption to the East-West Line on 25 September affected about 500,000 passenger journeys each day, out of 2.8 million daily train-based journeys, causing significant inconvenience to commuters.

sections.label: Track damage from incident train
sections.summary: Preliminary assessments found the incident train damaged 2.55 kilometres of track and trackside equipment including point machines, power cables, fasteners and third rails.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
sentences.text: Based on our preliminary assessments, the incident train caused damage to 2.55 kilometres of the track, as well as trackside equipment, including point machines, power cables, running rail fasteners and third rails.

sections.label: Shuttle services started
sections.summary: After confirming track safety, SMRT began shuttle services between Queenstown and Buona Vista, and Boon Lay and Jurong East, before the evening peak.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
sentences.text: After confirming that the tracks between these segments were safe, SMRT commenced shuttle services between Queenstown and Buona Vista stations, and between Boon Lay and Jurong East stations, at 3.56 pm and 4.11 pm respectively, ahead of the evening peak on 25 September.

sections.label: Bridging buses increased
sections.summary: By the evening peak, bridging buses rose from 39 to 70, with intervals of three to eight minutes, quicker than the 12 to 15 minute standards.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
sentences.text: By the evening peak, the number of bridging buses had also progressively increased from 39 before the peak period to 70, with an average interval of three to eight minutes, quicker than the stipulated service standards of 12 to 15 minutes for bridging bus services.

sections.label: Damaged rail segments replaced
sections.summary: 33 severely damaged rail segments over one tonne each needed replacement, and the public was told Jurong East to Buona Vista services would not resume next day.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
sentences.text: In addition, 33 severely damaged rail segments, each weighing more than one tonne, had to be replaced.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
sentences.text: Given the extent of the damage and with heavy rain preventing works at times, LTA and SMRT assessed that more time would be needed to safely complete the repair works.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
sentences.text: We informed the public at around 9.50 pm on 25 September that train services between Jurong East and Buona Vista would not resume the next day.

sections.label: Cracks found after tests
sections.summary: Stress and loading tests on 28 September evening found 12 new cracks on 10 unreplaced running rail segments before train services resumed.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
sentences.text: Stress and loading tests were then carried out in the evening of 28 September to ensure the tracks were functioning safely before resumption of train services.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
sentences.text: However, 12 new cracks, previously not visible to the naked eye, were detected on 10 unreplaced segments of running rail after these tests.

sections.label: Jurong East Buona Vista trains resume
sections.summary: Regular train services between Jurong East and Buona Vista stations resumed on the morning of Tuesday, 1 October.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
sentences.text: Regular train services between Jurong East and Buona Vista stations resumed on the morning of Tuesday, 1 October.

sections.label: LTA Expert Advisory Panel investigations
sections.summary: LTA will be supported by an Expert Advisory Panel chaired by Mr Malcolm Dobell, with investigations expected to be completed in the next few months and findings released publicly.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
sentences.text: To supplement its investigations, LTA will be supported by an Expert Advisory Panel (EAP), chaired by Mr Malcolm Dobell, former Head of Train Systems for the London Underground, and comprising five other local and overseas experts.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
sentences.text: I seek Members' understanding that more details will be shared when the investigations are completed.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
sentences.text: We expect the investigations to be completed in the next few months and the findings will be released publicly.

sections.label: KHI trains replaced by R151
sections.summary: The plan is to replace all KHI trains with new R151 trains by end-2026, and commuters exiting between Boon Lay and Queenstown were not charged.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
sentences.text: The plan is to replace all KHI trains with the new R151 trains by end-2026, before they reach their 38-year service mark.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
sentences.text: Train commuters exiting at stations between Boon Lay and Queenstown stations were not charged for their rail journeys.

sections.label: PTC defers fare increase quantum
sections.summary: PTC decided to defer most of the maximum allowable fare quantum and raise fares by 6% to keep fares affordable.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
sentences.text: Given the maximum allowable quantum of increase at 18.9% for this year's Exercise, due to the 15.6% balance carried over from last year, PTC decided to defer most of the maximum allowable fare quantum for this Exercise and raise fares by 6%, or less than one-third of the maximum quantum, to ensure that fares remain affordable for commuters.

sections.label: Overtime payment for LTA SMRT staff
sections.summary: LTA and SMRT staff who worked overtime will be given overtime payment accordingly.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
sentences.text: As for Mr Edward Chia's question about compensation for workers, LTA and SMRT staff that worked overtime will be given overtime payment accordingly.

sections.label: MKBF target achieved and maintained
sections.summary: LTA and operators achieved the MKBF target of at least one million train-kilometres in 2019 and have maintained it since for all MRT lines.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
sentences.text: Through the combined efforts of LTA and the operators and supported by our unions and workers, we achieved our MKBF target of at least one million train-kilometres in 2019 and have maintained that since for all MRT lines, including the East-West Line.

sections.label: MRT line reliability figures
sections.summary: Estimates show all MRT lines met the target of at least one million train-kilometres up to end-September 2024.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
sentences.text: The MKBF figures up to end-September 2024 have yet to be published, but the estimates show that all the MRT lines have achieved our target of at least one million train-kilometres: the East-West Line, 2.03 million; North-South Line, 1.42 million; North-East Line, 2.05 million; Circle Line, 1.04 million; and Downtown Line, 8.11 million.

sections.label: Circle Line and Jurong Region Line
sections.summary: Circle Line Stage 6 in 2026 and Jurong Region Line from 2027 to 2029 will improve West connectivity and interchanges.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
sentences.text: In 2026, when we "close the circle" with Stage 6 of the Circle Line, commuters in parts of the West will have another route to travel to the downtown area.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
sentences.text: The Jurong Region Line, which will open in three stages from 2027 to 2029, will also improve connectivity in the West and offer more alternative interchanges with the North-South and East-West lines at Chua Chu Kang, Boon Lay and Jurong East stations.

sections.label: Double-deck bus capacity limits
sections.summary: Double-deck buses carry up to 120 passengers at lower speeds, so 80 bridging buses could not match East-West Line capacity.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
sentences.text: In contrast, a double-deck bus carries up to 120 passengers and typically runs at much lower speeds, based on traffic conditions.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
sentences.text: Hence, even with up to 80 double-deck bridging buses deployed per day, these were unable to match the full capacity of the East-West Line.

sections.label: Disruption response and investigations
sections.summary: After the 25 September disruption was assessed, LTA and operators activated response plans, and investigations will be conducted.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
sentences.text: Once the scale of the disruption on 25 September was assessed, response plans from LTA and public transport operators were activated quickly, including the deployment of 80 bridging buses and hundreds of additional staff.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
sentences.text: LTA and the TSIB will conduct thorough investigations.

sections.label: Investigating East-West Line disruption
sections.summary: The team will investigate the 25 September East-West Line disruption, find its root cause, and review handling and recovery.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
sentences.text: Our team will continue to focus on ensuring that our MRT system remains safe, reliable and resilient.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
sentences.text: We will thoroughly investigate the disruption that occurred on the East-West Line on 25 September, ascertain the root cause of the incident, review the incident handling procedures, examine the service recovery efforts and identify areas for improvement.

sections.label: Ongoing MRT improvement mission
sections.summary: The incident was a setback but will not shake the determination to make the MRT safe, reliable and resilient.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
sentences.text: We will not stop here – improving safety, reliability and resilience is a key focus and an ongoing mission for us.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
sentences.text: This incident was a setback, Sir, but it will not shake our determination to do better and to make our MRT a safe, reliable and resilient rail system that Singaporeans can be proud of.

sections.label: MRT MKBF targets and East-West Line
sections.summary: The MRT network's MKBF rose from 67,000 train-kilometres in 2012 to the one million target in 2019, maintained since, including on the East-West Line.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: The MKBF for the MRT network was 67,000 train-kilometres in 2012 – I shared this earlier in my Statement.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: And we achieved our MKBF target of one million train-kilometres in 2019 and we have maintained that since for all the MRT lines.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: If we look at the East-West Line, its MKBF was 60,000 train-kilometres in 2012.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: It achieved the one million MKBF target in 2019 and it has maintained this even after accounting for the serious disruption in late September this year.

sections.label: Disruption response learning points
sections.summary: The response to the disruption incorporated learning points from previous episodes in communications, announcements, bridging bus services and signages.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: The response to this very serious disruption has incorporated some of the learning points from previous episodes in terms of communications, the announcements, the bridging bus services, the signages.

sections.label: Assistance for commuters needing help
sections.summary: The operating principle is to render more assistance to commuters who need more help, such as seniors, people with disabilities, and expectant mothers or those with young children.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: The operating principle that we will render more assistance to commuters who need more help, either because they are more vulnerable like seniors or people with disabilities, who need more help, or like in the case of what Ms Soh mentioned, mummies who are expecting or with young children, who may need more assistance.

sections.label: SAF activation not needed
sections.summary: The speaker says the SAF would support other Government agencies if activated, but assessed that activation was not needed for this incident, calling it the correct judgement call.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: But if we have to activate SAF – touch wood – I do not want that to happen too, I am sure the SAF will be there to support the other Government agencies for the benefit of Singapore and Singaporeans.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: But this is something that we assess for this particular incident, and I think it was the correct judgement call that we did not have to activate SAF for this.

sections.label: Expanding communication channels for breakdowns
sections.summary: A suggestion was made to consider expanding communication channels so vulnerable persons and caregivers are promptly notified of train breakdowns, which the speaker will discuss with LTA and operators.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Hua Han (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: In line of this, will the Government consider expanding the suite of communication channels available to ensure that as many vulnerable persons and their caregivers as possible are promptly notified when train breakdowns occur?

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: Certainly, I will take both suggestions back to discuss with LTA and the operators to see how we can do better.

sections.label: One million train-kilometres MKBF target
sections.summary: After international benchmarking comparisons, the decision was to set the target at one million train-kilometres MKBF, weighing high standards against sustaining costs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: High standards, versus the costs that we need to incur to sustain those high standards?

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: We have, after doing the international benchmarking comparisons, decided that the target that we want to set is one million train-kilometres MKBF.

sections.label: One million target maintained
sections.summary: All lines have maintained above one million since 2019, the current target.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: One million, which is our current target and, as I mentioned earlier, even though there are some differences between the different lines, all the lines have thus far maintained above one million since 2019.

sections.label: Operator maintenance spending assurance
sections.summary: The speaker lacks spending numbers but assures that both operators have not cut back on maintenance.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: I do not have the numbers with me in terms of the spending.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: But what I can assure Mr Chua and the House is that if we look at the spending over the past few years by the two operators, both of them have not cut back on maintenance.

sections.label: No deadline for EAP investigations
sections.summary: No deadline is given for the EAP or investigations, but the target is to complete them in a few months and release findings publicly.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: I do not want to give a deadline for the EAP or for the investigations, because I think we should let the process look through the necessary findings and evidence and for the experts to come to a decision on what they would then put forth to LTA for the investigations.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: But we have said that the target is to complete the investigations, which will include the views put forth by the EAP, in a few months and that the findings will be released publicly.

sections.label: LTA $2.6 billion renewal spending
sections.summary: LTA has mentioned before that it spent $2.6 billion on renewing the North-South and East-West Lines.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: My question is, I understand that LTA has mentioned before that it has spent $2.6 billion on the renewal of the North-South and East-West Lines.

sections.label: North-South East-West Lines renewal timeline
sections.summary: Renewal of the North-South and East-West Lines' systems started in 2012 and was substantially completed by October 2023.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: The renewal of the North-South and East-West Lines' systems started in 2012 and it was substantially completed by October 2023.

sections.label: East-West Line incident cause
sections.summary: The 25 September East-West Line incident was caused by a train fault, not a failure of core systems upgraded under the renewal programme.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: The 25 September East-West Line incident was caused by the train's axle box falling and then the wheels of one of the bogies shifted to the side of the rail; and this resulting in the incident train causing extensive damage to the tracks and the trackside equipment.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: So, this was due to a fault that was found on the train itself which is now the subject of investigation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: It was not caused by a failure of the core systems which were upgraded under the North-South and East-West Lines' renewal programme.

sections.label: New COI for breakdown
sections.summary: The Minister is asked whether a new COI would confirm the 2011 COI findings were implemented and consider non-technical factors.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: My second supplementary question: does the Minister think that a new COI for this breakdown as well would be useful for us to confirm that all the findings and the remedial actions recommended by the 2011 COI has been implemented till today, and whether there are any other new factors other than technical and engineering factors, like organisation factors, that we should take into account for the breakdown this time.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: So, that is the commitment that we have made to the public, that the investigations will be done thoroughly and the findings will be released publicly, and we will identify what are the root causes to the incident and what are the areas for improvement.

sections.label: Earlier COI findings implemented
sections.summary: The Minister says reliability improved from 60,000-plus MKBF to over one million MKBF for all lines, indicating earlier COI recommendations were implemented.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: Mr Leong asked whether the findings from the earlier COI have been put into practice.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: I would explain to Mr Leong that if we did not implement the recommendations for improvements since that COI due to the incident in 2011, I do not think our overall reliability could have improved from 60,000-plus MKBF in those days to more than one million MKBF for all lines today.

sections.label: Wait for investigation findings
sections.summary: The Minister says to wait for the investigations' findings and recommendations, and that the public transport vision remains unchanged.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: As to whether there are specific areas for further improvements that we need to make in response to this incident, I think let us wait for the conclusion of the investigations to see what the findings and recommendations are.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: I also want to reassure Mr Yip that the emphasis on walk, cycle, ride and public transport being the main mode of transport for Singapore and for Singaporeans, that vision, that target remains unchanged.

sections.label: Car-lite vision unchanged
sections.summary: The passage states the line will connect to the airport, Terminal Five and the Johor Bahru-Singapore RTS Link, and the car-lite vision remains unchanged.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: Eventually, it will connect to the airport, Terminal Five, and to the north, it will link up to the Johor Bahru-Singapore Rapid Transit System (RTS) Link when it is completed.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: So, the vision of a car-lite society, walk, cycle, ride, public transport being the main mode of transport, that remains unchanged.

sections.label: Service reliability incentives and penalties
sections.summary: The Minister says operators missing service quality or reliability benchmarks could miss incentive payments or face penalties after investigations.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: I accept that Mr Giam may have a different view, and I respect that, but I hope Mr Giam understands that we use different tools to achieve different objectives.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: So, for service reliability, we will keep track of the performance and if the operator were to miss their service quality benchmarks, their reliability benchmarks, they could miss out on receiving certain incentive payments or if there are lapses and investigations are conducted and there are lapses, they could also face penalties.

sections.label: Fare increases and service quality
sections.summary: The passage states that holding back fare increases and a chronic shortfall could further erode service quality and reliability.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: Because if you hold back on the fare increases which are supposed to reflect the overall operating costs facing the public transport system and there is a chronic shortfall over time, that could then further erode service quality and reliability, which I am sure we do not want to see happen.

sections.label: Opening delayed by one day
sections.summary: The opening was originally aimed at Monday, 30 September, but one more day was needed.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: Even though we took more time, originally, we were aiming for opening on Monday, 30 September; but in the end, we needed one more day.

sections.label: Worker involvement and tripartite partnership
sections.summary: Workers are involved in process improvements, and tripartite trust and partnership have helped the system improve from when MKBF was over 60,000 more than a decade ago.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: We also want to make sure that we involve our workers in making those process improvements and changes.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: This entire ecosystem approach, backed by strong tripartite trust and partnership, is something that has enabled our system to improve from the old days where MKBF was over 60,000 more than a decade ago to where we are today; and to go forward if we want to continue to maintain a safe, reliable and resilient public transport system.

sections.label: Safety checks and rail resilience
sections.summary: Questions covered safety spot checks during repairs, and the resilience plan includes expanding the rail network so commuters can switch lines during a disruption.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: For example, if they felt that there were some concerns around the working environment for their safety, whether there were any spot checks undertaken to ensure that all rules and safety guidelines were adhered to during the repair process?

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: I do not have a combined number for her, but each double-deck bus can carry up to 120 passengers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: Bridging buses alone, even including regular buses, can help to mitigate but not fully absorb the disruption caused by a rail system.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: This is why the game plan that we have to improve resilience includes an expansion of our rail network so that if there is going to be a disruption on one line, commuters can then switch to a different train line.

sections.label: Worker safety during day and night work
sections.summary: Worker safety is a key priority, with different teams taking shifts, rest in between, food and drinks, and proper safety equipment.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: Safety for workers is a key priority and we wanted to make sure that when they work day and night, it is not the same person working day and night, that there are different teams that can take shifts and that they are given rest in between, they are given food and drinks, they are given the proper safety equipment to enable them to work safely.

sections.label: Bus Connectivity Enhancement Programme funding
sections.summary: Bus rationalisation resources alone would not meet demand, so the Government announced the Bus Connectivity Enhancement Programme with up to $900 million over eight years.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: So, if we only rely on the resources that are re-allocated from bus rationalisation alone, that would not be enough to meet the demand.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: That is why the Government, earlier this year, announced that we are introducing the Bus Connectivity Enhancement Programme, where we will inject up to $900 million over the next eight years.

sections.label: Government subsidies for bus and rail
sections.summary: More than $1 billion a year is spent on bus subsidies and more than $1 billion on rail subsidies, with each commuter trip subsidised more than $1.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: Today, we spend every year, more than $1 billion on buses in terms of subsidies for commuters and more than $1 billion on rail in terms of subsidies for commuters.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: Every trip that is taken by a commuter carries with it a subsidy from the Government, more than $1.

sections.label: Predictive maintenance review request
sections.summary: A question asks whether the EAP will review if predictive maintenance systems are optimal, especially why an axle box failure was not predicted.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
sentences.text: During the disruption, some online commentators were understandably concerned that we have swung too far in relying on such predictive tools.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
sentences.text: So, I would like to ask the Minister if the EAP will review whether our current predictive maintenance systems are performing optimally, especially why it was not able to predict the occurrence of an axle box failure.

sections.label: Worker training and engineering scholarships
sections.summary: Over 3,000 workers have been trained, 700 more will be trained this year, and 25 scholarships and over 100 sponsorships awarded.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: More than 3,000 workers have been trained so far and another 700 workers will undergo similar training this year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: Second, we have scholarships and sponsorships to attract, retain and groom engineering talent within the industry.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: So far, we have awarded 25 undergraduate and polytechnic scholarships, and more than 100 in-service sponsorships.

sections.label: West Coast Extension study
sections.summary: LTA has been studying the West Coast Extension, which extends the Jurong Region Line to connect to the Circle Line.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: One of the projects which LTA has been studying is the implementation of the West Coast Extension.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: This involves extending the Jurong Region Line to connect to the Circle Line.

sections.label: Public hearings and LTA investigations
sections.summary: A Member asks if public hearings will be allowed, and the response describes LTA and TSIB investigations and an EAP of international and local experts.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazel Poa
sentences.text: So, would the Minister consider allowing such public hearings, because the transparency will be helpful towards building and maintaining public trust and confidence.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: And in the case of LTA, there will also be an EAP, comprising both international and local experts, and they will provide their inputs to LTA for the investigations.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: There are different ways to conduct an investigation, but if our objective in the end is to find out what happened, to ascertain the root causes and to identify the areas where we can do better, I am confident that what we have set out through the LTA and TSIB investigations can achieve that purpose.
